# Reap orphaned agent processes after the CLI is SIGKILLed / OOM-killed

## What to build

Bug KAN-67 / GE-06. When the `graph-execution` CLI dies from SIGKILL (or the OOM killer), the agent processes it started keep running. On POSIX each agent leads its own process group (`detached: true` in `src/providers/spawn.ts`), so it does not die with its parent. Nothing else will ever stop it: `--resume` and `graph-execution clean --yes` both leave it alive. SIGINT works, because `spawnAgent` kills the group on abort. Reproduced on this branch:

1. Start a run whose fake task 1 hangs: `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT` = `{"task:1":{"attempts":[{"hang":true}]}}`.
2. Wait for `.graph-execution/<run>/worktrees/task-1-a1/.fake-agent.pid`.
3. `kill -9 $(cat .graph-execution/<run>/lock)`.

The agent is now reparented to PID 1 and stays alive, and `state.json` keeps `status: "running"` with task 1 `running`. `graph-execution --resume` then finishes the run with exit 0, but the old agent is **still alive**. `graph-execution clean --yes` deletes the run folder and the worktree, and the agent is **still alive** too, now in a deleted cwd.

Build a small process registry:

- **Record.** Every agent process `spawnAgent` starts is recorded in a file `<runDir>/pids/<pid>.json` the moment it is spawned. The record holds its pid, process-group id, start time (to guard against pid reuse), label and role, and the owning CLI's pid and start time. The file is deleted when the agent exits. Writes are synchronous, so a SIGKILL right after the spawn still leaves the record on disk.
- **Reap.** A new `reapOrphans(dir)` finds records whose owner is dead and kills their process groups that are still alive: SIGTERM, a short grace period, then SIGKILL. It checks the start time before killing, so it never kills a process that merely reuses a recorded pid. It runs on `--resume` (before `reconcile` removes worktrees), on `suite --resume` (for the suite's own integration/e2e agents), and in `clean` (before the worktrees and folder are deleted).

The existing `reconcile` (`src/state/resume.ts`) already turns `running`/`validating` tasks back to `pending` on resume, and `list` already shows a dead run as `unfinished`, so no state-schema change is needed.

Linux and macOS are required. On Windows this is best-effort: there are no process groups there, so the record is still written and `reapOrphans` kills the recorded pid's tree with `taskkill /T /F`, but only when the image name still matches the recorded command.

This task builds on the agent-timeout task already merged into `src/providers/spawn.ts`. That file now also passes `stdout: capLines(), stderr: capLines()` to execa and exports `MAX_LINE_CHARS`/`capLines`, and `src/agents/idle.ts` has a `watchIdle` provider wrapper that run.ts, e2e.ts and integrate.ts wrap around `watchLoops`. Keep all of that; only add to it. Re-read the current files before you edit them, because line numbers below are from before that task and may have moved a few lines.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `src/providers/spawn.ts` (whole file, ~90–130 lines) — `SpawnOptions` (lines 4–13), `killTree` (lines 35–45, POSIX `process.kill(-pid, "SIGTERM")`, Windows `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`), `spawnAgent` (lines 58–92): `child.pid`, abort listener, and the `exitCode` promise where the group is signalled again on exit (line 83 `if (!WINDOWS) kill();`). Add the spawn/exit hooks here.
- `src/providers/types.ts` (lines 1–33) — `AgentRunOptions`, which every adapter spreads into `spawnAgent`'s options: `spawnAgent(CLAUDE_BIN, claudeArgs(opts), { ...opts, input: opts.prompt })` (claude.ts:55, codex.ts:44, opencode.ts:41, qwen.ts:45), and the fake passes `opts` straight through (fake.ts:126 and 141). A new optional field on `AgentRunOptions` therefore reaches `spawnAgent` with no adapter changes, as long as `SpawnOptions` declares it too.
- `src/agents/loop.ts` (lines 86–133) — `watchLoops`, the provider-wrapper pattern (`provider.run({ ...opts, … })`); `watchIdle` in `src/agents/idle.ts` follows it too.
- `src/state/state.ts` (lines 160–201) — `LOCK_FILE`, `isAlive(pid)` (EPERM counts as alive), `lockHolder`, `acquireLock`: the lock file holds the CLI's pid. A SIGKILLed CLI leaves `lock` with a dead pid, which `acquireLock` takes over.
- `src/runner/run.ts` — line 61 (`watchLoops` import, `watchIdle` next to it); the provider chain in `execute` at ~lines 259–270 (`teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(ctx.provider, …)))`); `resume()` at lines 209–245: `acquireLock(runDir)` at line 216, `log(\`resuming run …\`)` at line 226, `await reconcile(state, repo, runDir)` at line 227; `prepareRetry` at line 572 also calls `reconcile` in-process (must NOT reap: same owner).
- `src/state/resume.ts` (lines 35–109) — `reconcile`: removes every task worktree and resets `running` tasks to `pending`. Reaping must happen before it.
- `src/suite/orchestrator.ts` (lines 195–215) — `resumeSuite`: `acquireLock(suiteDir)` at line 199; reap `suiteDir` right after it. Feature runs are separate CLI processes resumed with `--resume --run <id>` (line 293), so they reap through `resume()`.
- `src/suite/e2e.ts` (lines 75–90) and `src/suite/integrate.ts` (lines 115–130) — the suite-level provider chains (`teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(env.provider, …)))`); `suiteDir` is in scope in both.
- `src/cleanup/execute.ts` (lines 1–37) — `execute(repo, plan, log)`: for each entry with a `dir`, it removes worktrees (also `features/<f>/worktrees` for suites), branches, then the folder. Reap before line 19 `await pruneWorktrees(repo)`.
- `src/cleanup/scan.ts` (lines 75–98) — `kind: "live"` when `lockHolder(dir)` is alive; `plan` never puts a live run into a clean plan, so `execute` only sees runs whose CLI is dead.
- `src/providers/fake.ts` (lines 16–20, 120–146) — `hang` spawns a real node child through `spawnAgent(..., opts)` that writes `.fake-agent.pid` (its own pid) into its cwd; `orphan` leaves a background process in the agent's group.
- `src/cli.test.ts` (lines 1–20 and 95–127) — the "on SIGINT kills the running agent" test: runs the built `dist/cli.js` with a hang script, waits for the pid file, signals the CLI. Copy it for SIGKILL. `withRepo` is defined in that file.
- `src/providers/spawn.test.ts` (lines 1–63) — spawnAgent test style.
- `README.md` (lines 121–131 "What a run produces", lines 432–447 "Resume", lines 363–377 "Cleaning up runs").

## Patterns to follow

**Process start time (verified on this Linux box: `/proc/<pid>/stat` field 22; macOS `ps -o lstart=`):**
```typescript
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

/** An opaque start-time token for `pid`, undefined when it is gone or unknown (Windows). Same pid + same token = same process. */
export function processStartTime(pid: number): string | undefined {
  try {
    if (process.platform === "linux") {
      const stat = readFileSync(`/proc/${pid}/stat`, "utf8");
      // Fields after the `(comm)`, which may contain spaces: index 0 is field 3 (state), index 19 is field 22 (starttime).
      return stat.slice(stat.lastIndexOf(")") + 2).split(" ")[19];
    }
    if (process.platform === "win32") return undefined;
    const out = execFileSync("ps", ["-o", "lstart=", "-p", String(pid)], { encoding: "utf8", stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"] }).trim();
    return out || undefined;
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}
```

**Group liveness (POSIX):** a process-group id cannot be reused as a pid while that group still has members. So `kill(-pgid, 0)` succeeding means the group we recorded still exists, even after its leader died:
```typescript
function groupAlive(pgid: number): boolean {
  try { process.kill(-pgid, 0); return true; } catch (err) { return (err as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code === "EPERM"; }
}
```

**Provider wrapper (src/agents/loop.ts:91-104):**
```typescript
export function watchLoops(provider: Provider, settings: LoopSettings, onLoop?: …): Provider {
  if (settings === false) return provider;
  return {
    name: provider.name,
    run(opts): AgentRun {
      …
      const agent = provider.run({ ...opts, signal: own.signal });
```

**Error handling:** bookkeeping must never fail an agent or a run. Wrap every registry read/write/unlink in `try { … } catch { /* ignore */ }`, as `killTree` does (spawn.ts:39-43).

**Test pattern (src/cli.test.ts:95-127):**
```typescript
const child = execa("node", [cli, fixture("diamond"), "--spec", spec, "--provider", "fake"], {
  cwd: repo, env: { GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT: script }, reject: false,
});
// poll for <runDir>/worktrees/task-1-a1/.fake-agent.pid, read agentPid
child.kill("SIGINT");
const res = await child;
expect(() => process.kill(agentPid, 0)).toThrow();
```

**Naming / file conventions:** state helpers live in `src/state/`, tests next to the source as `<name>.test.ts`, ESM `.js` import suffixes.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `src/providers/types.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add
  ```typescript
  /** Told about every OS process an agent run starts, so a killed CLI's agents can be found later (`src/state/processes.ts`). */
  export interface ProcessHooks {
    started(pid: number, command: string): void;
    exited(pid: number): void;
  }
  ```
  and an optional `processHooks?: ProcessHooks;` on `AgentRunOptions`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### UPDATE `src/providers/spawn.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: add `processHooks?: ProcessHooks` to `SpawnOptions`. Right after `execa(...)` returns, if `child.pid !== undefined`, call `opts.processHooks?.started(child.pid, file)`, synchronously and before anything is awaited. In the `exitCode` promise, after `await killing` (that is, after the POSIX group re-kill at line 83 or the Windows taskkill), call `opts.processHooks?.exited(child.pid)`. Wrap both calls in try/catch so a hook can never break the spawn. Update the doc comment: the process is reported to `processHooks` so a later `--resume`/`clean` can kill it if this CLI dies without cleaning up.
- **IMPORTS**: `import type { ProcessHooks } from "./types.js";`
- **GOTCHA**: keep `stdout: capLines(), stderr: capLines()` and everything else the timeout task added. The fake and real adapters pass `AgentRunOptions` through, so no adapter file changes. Do not call `exited` on the "failed to start" path when no pid exists.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/providers/spawn.test.ts`

### CREATE `src/state/processes.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - `export const PIDS_DIR = "pids";` and `export const pidsDir = (runDir: string) => path.join(runDir, PIDS_DIR);`
  - `export interface ProcessRecord { pid: number; pgid: number; start?: string; command: string; label: string; role: string; owner: number; ownerStart?: string; }`. `pgid` equals `pid` on POSIX, because the agent leads its own group.
  - `processStartTime(pid)` as shown above, and `groupAlive(pgid)`.
  - `recordProcess(runDir, rec)`: `mkdirSync(pidsDir, { recursive: true })`, then `writeFileSync(<pid>.json, JSON.stringify(rec))`. `forgetProcess(runDir, pid)`: `rmSync(<pid>.json, { force: true })`. Both are synchronous and swallow errors.
  - `export function trackProcesses(provider: Provider, runDir: string): Provider`: returns `{ name: provider.name, run: (opts) => provider.run({ ...opts, processHooks: { started: (pid, command) => recordProcess(runDir, { pid, pgid: pid, start: processStartTime(pid), command, label: opts.label, role: opts.role, owner: process.pid, ownerStart: processStartTime(process.pid) }), exited: (pid) => forgetProcess(runDir, pid) } }) }`. Compute `ownerStart` once per process, not per spawn.
  - `export async function reapOrphans(dir: string, opts: { log?: (line: string) => void; graceMs?: number } = {}): Promise<ProcessRecord[]>` reads every `*.json` in `pidsDir(dir)`, skipping unreadable or invalid files, and for each record:
    1. If `rec.owner === process.pid`, or the owner is alive (`isAlive(owner)`, and `processStartTime(owner) === rec.ownerStart` when both are known), skip it and keep the file: a live CLI still owns it.
    2. POSIX: if `!groupAlive(rec.pgid)`, delete the file (already gone). If the leader is alive but `rec.start` is set and `processStartTime(rec.pid) !== rec.start`, the pid was reused by something else: delete the file and do not kill. Otherwise `process.kill(-rec.pgid, "SIGTERM")`, poll `groupAlive` every 50 ms for up to `graceMs` (default 2000), then `process.kill(-rec.pgid, "SIGKILL")` if the group is still there. Delete the file, add the record to the result, and `log?.(\`stopped agent ${rec.label} (pid ${rec.pid}) left running by an earlier graph-execution process\`)`.
    3. Windows: if `isAlive(rec.pid)` and the image name from `tasklist /FI "PID eq <pid>" /FO CSV /NH` contains `path.parse(rec.command).name`, run `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F`. Delete the file either way.
    Wrap every kill in try/catch (ESRCH means it is already gone). Return the reaped records.
- **IMPORTS**: `node:fs` (`mkdirSync, readFileSync, rmSync, writeFileSync`), `node:fs/promises` (`readdir, readFile`), `node:child_process` (`execFileSync`), `node:path`, `execa` (for taskkill/tasklist, as spawn.ts does), `isAlive` from `./state.js`, `type { Provider }` from `../providers/types.js`.
- **GOTCHA**: never kill a group without the start-time guard when `rec.start` is known. Never reap records owned by the current process (`prepareRetry` → `reconcile` runs in-process with live agents). A zombie still answers `kill(pid, 0)`, so do not wait for confirmed death after SIGKILL: send it and move on.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### CREATE `src/state/processes.test.ts` (skip the file on win32: `describe.skipIf(process.platform === "win32")`)

- **IMPLEMENT**:
  - **Dead owner → reaped.** `const child = spawn(process.execPath, ["-e", "setInterval(() => {}, 1 << 30)"], { detached: true, stdio: "ignore" })`, so it leads its own group like an agent. Make a dead owner pid with `spawnSync(process.execPath, ["-e", ""]).pid` (exited and reaped). `recordProcess(dir, { pid: child.pid, pgid: child.pid, start: processStartTime(child.pid), command: process.execPath, label: "1", role: "task", owner: deadPid })`. Await `reapOrphans(dir, { graceMs: 500 })`. Expect it to return one record with label `"1"`, the child to have exited (`await once(child, "exit")` resolves with signal `SIGTERM`), and `pids/<pid>.json` to be gone.
  - **A grandchild in the same group is killed too:** the child spawns its own `setInterval` child without `detached` and prints its pid. After the reap, poll until `process.kill(grandPid, 0)` throws, up to 5 s.
  - **Live owner → untouched:** `owner: process.pid` → nothing returned, the child is still alive, and the record is kept.
  - **Pid reuse guard:** `start: "not-the-real-start"` with a dead owner → nothing killed (the child is still alive), and the record is deleted.
  - **Already gone:** a record for an exited pid → removed, nothing returned.
  - **trackProcesses + spawnAgent:** `createFakeProvider(fakeScriptSchema.parse({ "task:1": { attempts: [{ hang: true }] } }), { onSpawn })` wrapped in `trackProcesses(provider, dir)`, with a temp `cwd`. In `onSpawn(pid)`, expect `<dir>/pids/<pid>.json` to exist with `owner: process.pid` and `pgid: pid`. Then abort the signal, await `done`, and expect the file to be gone.
  - Kill every spawned child in `afterEach` (try/catch) and remove the temp dirs.
- **PATTERN**: `src/providers/spawn.test.ts` (mkdtemp + realpath, real node children).
- **IMPORTS**: `node:child_process` (`spawn, spawnSync`), `node:events` (`once`), `node:fs` (`existsSync`), `node:fs/promises` (`mkdtemp, rm, realpath`), `node:os` (`tmpdir`), `vitest`, `./processes.js`, `../providers/fake.js`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/state/processes.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/runner/run.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: (1) In `execute`, make `trackProcesses(ctx.provider, ctx.runDir)` the innermost provider, so the chain is `teeOutput(watchIdle(watchLoops(trackProcesses(ctx.provider, ctx.runDir), …), …), events)`. (2) In `resume()`, right after `acquireLock(runDir)` (line 216) and before `reconcile` (line 227): `await reapOrphans(runDir, { log });`. (3) Do NOT reap in `prepareRetry`.
- **IMPORTS**: `import { reapOrphans, trackProcesses } from "../state/processes.js";`
- **GOTCHA**: `startFailureSummaries` gets the same `provider`, so summarizer processes are tracked too (their cwd is `<runDir>/summaries/work`, but the record goes to `<runDir>/pids`).
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/runner/run.test.ts src/state/resume.test.ts`

### UPDATE `src/suite/e2e.ts`, `src/suite/integrate.ts`, `src/suite/orchestrator.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in e2e.ts and integrate.ts, replace `env.provider` inside the chain with `trackProcesses(env.provider, suiteDir)`. In `resumeSuite` (orchestrator.ts), right after `const release = await acquireLock(suiteDir);` at line 199, at the start of the `try`: `await reapOrphans(suiteDir, { log });`.
- **IMPORTS**: `import { reapOrphans, trackProcesses } from "../state/processes.js";` (only what each file uses).
- **GOTCHA**: when a suite CLI itself is SIGKILLed, its feature-run CLIs are separate processes that hold their own locks. They are live runs and are not reaped here. Out of scope.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx tsc --noEmit`

### UPDATE `src/cleanup/execute.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: for every entry with `entry.kind !== "orphans" && entry.dir`, before `await pruneWorktrees(repo)` (line 19): `await reapOrphans(entry.dir, { log })`, and for suites also `reapOrphans(path.join(featuresDir, f), { log })` for each feature folder. That means building the list of run folders (`entry.dir` plus `features/<f>`) next to the `dirs` list of worktree folders at lines 14–18.
- **IMPORTS**: `import { reapOrphans } from "../state/processes.js";`
- **GOTCHA**: `plan` already keeps live runs out, so every owner here is dead; `reapOrphans` still re-checks it.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/cleanup`

### UPDATE `src/cli.test.ts`

- **IMPLEMENT**: two tests next to "on SIGINT kills the running agent…" (line 95), using the same setup.
  - **"after a SIGKILL, --resume stops the agent the killed run left running":** start the run with the hang script and wait for `.fake-agent.pid` (agentPid). Expect `<runDir>/pids/<agentPid>.json` to exist. `child.kill("SIGKILL"); await child;`. Expect the agent to be still alive (`process.kill(agentPid, 0)` does not throw). Write `{}` to the script file, so the resumed task succeeds. Run `node dist/cli.js --resume` in the repo with `GRAPH_EXECUTION_FAKE_SCRIPT` set to it. Expect exit 0, stdout to contain `stopped agent 1 (pid ${agentPid})`, the agent to be gone (poll, see GOTCHA), and `<runDir>/pids` to have no `.json` files left.
  - **"after a SIGKILL, clean --yes stops the agent before deleting the run":** same start and SIGKILL, then `node dist/cli.js clean --yes`. Expect exit 0, the agent gone, and the run folder deleted.
- **GOTCHA**: the agent is not this test's child. After the kill it is reparented to PID 1, so poll for up to 5 s with a helper that counts a zombie as gone: `process.kill(pid, 0)` throws, or on Linux `/proc/<pid>/stat`'s state field is `Z`. The fake script's attempts restart at index 0 in a new process, which is why the script is rewritten to `{}` before `--resume`. The run-config hashes do not include the fake script. `dist/` is built by `vitest.global-setup.ts`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/cli.test.ts -t SIGKILL`

### UPDATE `README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in "What a run produces" (lines 123–131) add `  pids/                               # agent processes still running (removed as they exit)`. In "Resume" (bullets at lines 441–445) add: "If the run's process was killed without a chance to clean up (`kill -9`, the OOM killer), the agents it left running are stopped first: each agent's pid, process group and start time are recorded in `pids/` while it runs, and a recorded agent whose owner is gone is killed with its whole process group. A pid that now belongs to another process is never touched. Windows: best effort." In "Cleaning up runs" (after the table, line ~377) add: "`clean` stops such leftover agents too, before deleting their worktrees."
- **VALIDATE**: `npx vitest run src/readme`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] While an agent runs, `<runDir>/pids/<pid>.json` exists with `pid`, `pgid`, `start`, `command`, `label`, `role`, `owner` (the CLI's pid) and `ownerStart`. It is removed when the agent exits, on success, failure, abort (SIGINT) or idle/loop stop.
- [ ] After `kill -9` of the CLI during a hanging fake task, `graph-execution --resume` logs `stopped agent 1 (pid <n>) left running by an earlier graph-execution process`, the old agent and its process group are gone, and the run finishes (exit 0 with a non-hanging script).
- [ ] After the same kill, `graph-execution clean --yes` kills the agent, then deletes the worktrees and the run folder.
- [ ] Records owned by a live process (another live CLI, or this process during in-process Retry) are never reaped.
- [ ] A recorded pid whose start time no longer matches is not killed; its record is dropped.
- [ ] Suite resume reaps the suite folder's own integration/e2e agent records.
- [ ] Linux and macOS are covered by tests; on Windows the tests are skipped and the code is best-effort and never throws.
- [ ] Tests pass: `npx vitest run src/state/processes.test.ts src/providers/spawn.test.ts src/cli.test.ts src/cleanup src/state/resume.test.ts src/runner/run.test.ts`

## Validation commands

```bash
# Type / lint
npx tsc --noEmit && npx eslint .

# Tests for this slice
npx vitest run src/state/processes.test.ts src/providers/spawn.test.ts src/providers/fake.test.ts src/cleanup src/state/resume.test.ts src/runner/run.test.ts src/runner/run-retry.test.ts
npx vitest run src/cli.test.ts -t "SIGKILL|SIGINT"
```
